featured_reviews.review_text:
Having heard reviews about this tiny but interesting joint at Charni Road serving Locho, we decided to go there a few days ago. Needless to say, it was extremely tiny with seating for just 5 people at max.

The menu showed pizzas, wraps, fries and a few other stuff too along with a wide variety of Locho but we decided to go with what the place is known for. Everything in the menu, we were told, could be made Jain, except for what was expressly named as containing garlic. We tried the basic oil Locho and butter garlic Locho, both of which were good and quite distinct in taste. I would give the butter locho a slightly upper hand for its flavours and along with the Sev on top and chopped onion and green chutney served alongside, it tasted delicious. Would surely come back again for it when Locho cravings strike back!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Govinda's Restaurant near Chowpatty, Girgaon, and had a wonderful dining experience. What makes this place truly unique is that, being associated with the ISKCON Temple Trust, they do not use garlic or onions in any of their preparations. Despite this, the food is incredibly flavorful and satisfying, proving that great taste doesn't always need conventional ingredients.

The menu offers a wide variety of options across different cuisines. We started our meal with a selection of soups including Artichoke Bisque, Minestrone, Manchow, Tomato Lemongrass, and Laksa Soup. Each soup had a distinct flavor profile and was perfectly balanced. My personal favorite was the Artichoke Bisque Soup, as it was my first time trying it and I absolutely loved its rich, creamy texture and unique taste.

For starters, we ordered the Kung Pao Paneer and Masala Papad. The paneer was well-cooked with just the right amount of spice, while the masala papad made for a light and crunchy accompaniment.

In the main course, we enjoyed Paneer Lababdar and Dal Tadka paired with Jeera Rice. The gravies were comforting, flavorful, and complemented the rice beautifully.

The highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the Sizzling Brownie. Served hot and indulgent, it was the perfect way to end the dining experience.

Overall, Govinda's is a small yet charming restaurant with a constant flow of patrons, which speaks volumes about its popularity. If you're looking for delicious vegetarian food with a unique sattvic approach, this place is definitely worth a visit.

featured_reviews.name: Azim Hannure
featured_reviews.review_text:
Santosh Sagar Fast Food is a popular eatery known for its delicious, freshly prepared dishes and quick service. Located in a convenient and lively area, it attracts both locals and visitors looking for tasty and affordable meals. The menu offers a wide variety of options, including South Indian favorites like dosa, idli, and uttapam, as well as North Indian snacks, Chinese dishes, and refreshing beverages. Each item is prepared with good quality ingredients and served hot, ensuring a satisfying dining experience.

The restaurant has a clean and casual ambiance, making it perfect for families, friends, and even solo diners. The service is prompt, and the staff are friendly, polite, and attentive to customer needs. One of the highlights of Santosh Sagar Fast Food is its consistency — whether you visit for breakfast, lunch, or dinner, the taste and quality remain the same.

Prices are quite reasonable, offering great value for money, and the portion sizes are generous. It’s an excellent choice for a quick bite or a relaxed meal without compromising on flavor. Overall, Santosh Sagar Fast Food is a reliable and well-loved spot that delivers on taste, hygiene, and affordability — a true favorite among food lovers.

Review: Soam Restaurant, Mumbai

We stay in Chembur and our family visited Soam restaurant in SoBo for the first time and enjoyed a truly satisfying vegetarian dining experience.

We ordered a wide spread of dishes — panki, sev puri, dahi puri, dahi bhalla chaat, watana ghughra, sada dosa, aloo puri with potato subji, thepla with red potato subji, moong dal khichadi and kadhi. Each item was flavorful, well‑prepared, and appreciated by everyone at the table.

The service was prompt and courteous, making the meal smooth and enjoyable. The atmosphere was decent, not extraordinary, but comfortable enough for a relaxed family outing.

One point worth noting is the pricing. Compared to similar restaurants in the suburbs, Soam is on the higher side. Perhaps this is the premium for being a very popular SoBo (South Bombay) restaurant.

Overall, Soam impressed us with its authentic flavors and variety. It’s a place we would recommend to anyone looking for wholesome vegetarian food in South Mumbai, while keeping in mind the pricing.

customer_updates.text:
Visited Benne after hearing a lot of hype, but honestly, it didn’t live up to expectations at all. Everything we tried was pretty mid — not bad, but nothing stood out or felt worth the hype. The food was decent, just very average in terms of taste and presentation, and nothing really made me want to come back for more.

featured_reviews.name: Priyanka Dhruv
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Benne and had a really lovely experience. The space is very spacious with a minimal, clean aesthetic, and the high ceilings make the entire restaurant feel even more beautiful and open.

What truly stood out to me was how thoughtfully they care for senior citizens. I was visiting with my parents, and the staff was incredibly attentive, patient, and considerate towards them, which made the experience even more comfortable and special.

We tried the Benne Masala, Benne Podi Masala, Idli, and Idli vada, everything was delicious and well-prepared. The chutneys truly stood out and complemented the dishes perfectly. We also had their filter coffee and the filter coffee soft serve, both of which were excellent and worth trying.

The staff was extremely attentive and helpful throughout, and the separate coffee station was a great touch. The girl preparing our coffee was especially warm and sweet, which added to the overall experience.

The washrooms were neat and clean, which is always appreciated. Overall, it’s a great place for a unique, quick dining experience that still feels comfortable and relaxed.

Would definitely visit again!

featured_reviews.review_text: Too good! I’m already a fan of this place and this branch just made me like it even more. The seating area is much bigger and comfortable. featured_reviews.name: Azeem khan
featured_reviews.review_text: Boy oh boy! What an amazing dosa. I tried their benne ghee pudi masala dosa (200 rupees) and it was the best dosa I have ever had in my life. I have tried a lots of dosa in my life be it Rameshwaram be it Carnatic cafe be it  Naivedyam etc. But this one is by far the best. Such rich tast and flavor exploding in your mouth as you devour your meal is just amazing. The staff is super professional and as polite as an angel, extremely helpful and the atmosphere is sooooo amazing with pleasant vibes and premium and hygienic washrooms. They do not use plastic at all even the plastic bags they use for trash are biodegradable. They have water bottles and cups everywhere for the customers and in the center of the cafe They have a bar like counter where they serve desserts and beverages, they also serve cold filter coffee. Their hot chocolate ice cream fudge is also very amazing. Comming back to the dosa, their gunpowder masala is completely out of the world never tasted something like this and they don't server sambar but you know what it still tastes crazy even without sambar their rich and flavourful green and red chutney steals the show. There is a queue for most of the times just to get the entry to this cafe but it is so worth it must try dosa place 5/5 from me.

featured_reviews.name: chirag shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Benne Chowpatty is a huge and beautifully designed place with a great variety of food options. The food quality is genuinely excellent, and that is what makes the place worth visiting. Every dish we tried was flavorful and enjoyable.

However, one major issue is car parking, which can be quite inconvenient, especially during peak hours. Another drawback is that the place is extremely crowded and noisy. I personally would not recommend it for large groups, because everyone cannot sit or stand together comfortably, and having proper conversations becomes difficult. It feels more like “eat and leave” rather than a relaxed outing.

Even after paying premium prices, still have to stand while eating, which may not be comfortable for everyone.

One more thing I noticed was that although there are many staff members around to help, there is no proper dress code, uniform, or identification badge, so it becomes difficult to recognize who actually belongs to the restaurant staff.

Overall, the food is truly impressive and worth trying, but the overall dining experience could improve a lot with better crowd management, seating arrangements, parking facilities, and proper staff identification.

featured_reviews.name: Dd 9
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is a lovely new dosa spot that’s opened at Chowpatty, near Marine Drive. The first outlet was in Bandra, a much smaller space that always had long queues. This one is far bigger, so the wait should ideally be shorter.

The place
The space is done up really well, high ceilings, warm lighting, and a very inviting vibe overall.

Food
The menu is short and well thought through. The benne dosas are excellent, while not drastically different from places like Rameshwaram, they’re definitely a notch better. The idlis were soft and really good, and the desserts were impressive too. (The Mysore Pak was sold out when I went, unfortunately.) They have bournvita too for the kids and adults who like it

Staff
The staff is polite and well-mannered, and the owner seemed to be personally present, which always adds a nice touch. Hope this remains as it is.  As with time staff gets rude and more complacent

If the waiting time is under 15 minutes, it’s absolutely worth trying. Good stuff. Although i wish i wanted to have some more south Indian delicacies in the menu

featured_reviews.name: RAHUL V
featured_reviews.review_text:
Benne Vo… probably the best dosa I’ve ever tried! 🤤

And finally, I’m here at Benne to check if the hype is real or not…

As soon as you enter, you’ll spot a digital ordering machine on the left where you can place your order easily. Their menu is simple and limited — but trust me, that’s a good sign 👀

Here’s what I ordered:
✨ Benne Masala Dosa
✨ Ghee Podi Idli
✨ Benne Fudge
✨ Mysore Pak
✨ Filter Coffee

They have separate counters for everything — dosa, beverages, desserts — and even a special chutney bar to refill your chutneys 🤍

There’s also a huge screen displaying your order status, which makes the whole experience super smooth.

Now let’s talk about the food 😭❤️

The dosa was insanely good — crispy outside, buttery, and the potato filling was perfectly flavorful.

The Ghee Podi Idli was HUGE! But honestly, once I started eating it, I just wanted more and more 🤌 The softness and texture were outstanding.

The Mysore Pak was super fresh, soft, and literally melted in my mouth.

But the real winner for me was the Benne Fudge 😍
The yummiest dessert I’ve had in a long time. I’m definitely going back again and again just for that!

And guess what…?
The hype is ACTUALLY REAL ✅

featured_reviews.review_text:
The concept of a high tea unlimited buffet would seem attractive to the Indian pallet. Most food items like the two bite burger or the singal piece sev puri are certainly not items to be eaten cold and stale in a buffet.
The service was pleasent but excruciatingly slow for the 90 plus year old ladies who visited more for the experience than to demonstrate their poor appetite. The only item that they thought would be worth having with a hot coffee or tea were the bhajiyas.

And, the staff tested the ladies patience of taking almost 30 minutes plus to heat and serve them. Thank God the flavour of the mango mousse in the tiny cutting chai glass was the saving grace for these oldies. But, at ₹725/- (including taxes) per person this was certainly more premium a price for being next to the Bhavan's and Wilson College clientele than the food, service or lounging.

While the decore has some antique stuff like the ancient telephone ... overall they have the opportunity to work a lot on the atmosphere too.

If you're looking for a hearty and satisfying breakfast, then the nashta at Dave's is a must-try. The store serves a variety of nashta dishes, including khaman, dhokla, and fafda, all made with fresh ingredients and bursting with flavor.

Dave's samosas are another favorite among regular customers. The crispy, golden pastry is stuffed with a delicious mixture of spiced potatoes and peas, making for a mouth-watering snack that's perfect for any time of day.

The store also serves a range of other Gujarati specialties, including dhoklas, khandvis, and undhiyu. Each dish is made with care and attention to detail, ensuring that you get the authentic taste of Gujarati cuisine.

What sets Dave's apart is its commitment to using only the freshest and highest quality ingredients. The store also takes great care in preparing each dish, ensuring that you get the best possible taste and flavor in every bite.
